picasso.description: From the Suite Vollard, plate G.208, catalogued by Georges Bloch (Vol. I, no. 141). Etched on 10 April 1933 and signed in pencil. Printed by Lacourière and published by Ambroise Vollard, Paris.
picasso.blurb: One of the hundred prints of the Suite Vollard, the series Picasso etched between 1930 and 1937 and widely regarded as the pinnacle of his graphic work. Clean, classical line turns an everyday gesture into a small, intimate theatre. A museum piece on a domestic scale.

dominguez.style: Cubist · 'Vistas urbanas de una ciudad irreal' series
dominguez.description: Oil painting from the series 'Vistas urbanas de una ciudad irreal' (Urban views of an unreal city). Certified by Ana Vázquez de Parga and registered with the Museo TEA.
dominguez.blurb: An oil from Óscar Domínguez's Parisian period — the Canarian Surrealist who invented decalcomania. In the series «Vistas urbanas de una ciudad irreal», architecture breaks down into Cubist-rooted planes within a dreamlike atmosphere. Certified and registered with TEA, Tenerife.

tapies-sin-titulo.description: Original painting on paper, signed lower right. Here Tàpies sets out his matter-based language with expressionist gashes and rough impasto.
tapies-sin-titulo.blurb: Original painting on paper signed by Antoni Tàpies in 1976, at the height of his maturity. Gashes, rough impasto and pencil build a surface that reads like a wall: the matter-based language that made Tàpies a central figure of post-war European art.

tapies-ulleres.medium: Paint and pencil on brown wrapping paper
tapies-ulleres.description: Registered in the artist's complete works archive (Foto T-9239). Paint on brown wrapping paper.
tapies-ulleres.blurb: A unique work registered in the Tàpies complete works archive. Humble, absorbent wrapping paper takes paint and pencil as if it were a wall marked by time. A piece that sums up his fondness for poor materials and everyday signs.

barcelo.description: Work certified by Galerie Bruno Bischofberger AG, Zurich (2010). In 2009 the artist represented Spain at the Venice Biennale.
barcelo.blurb: Gouache on paper from 1988, certified by Galerie Bruno Bischofberger in Zurich, one of the leading galleries of international contemporary art. Direct painting, with swift gesture and living matter, by one of the most acclaimed living Spanish artists.

barcelo-lanzarote.description: Etching from the Lanzarote series by Miquel Barceló, one of the most internationally acclaimed living Spanish artists. The series captures the volcanic, organic force of the Lanzarote landscape in Barceló's characteristic matter-based, gestural language.
barcelo-lanzarote.blurb: Etching from the Lanzarote series, in an edition of 35. Barceló transfers his physical relationship with landscape and matter onto the copper plate: a print of great presence, with the energy of drawing and the depth of intaglio black.

warhol-stocking.edition: Authenticated by The Andy Warhol Foundation for The Visual Arts
warhol-stocking.description: Offset lithograph from Warhol's early years as a commercial illustrator. Authenticated by the Andy Warhol Foundation and bearing the Estate of Andy Warhol stamp on the verso.
warhol-stocking.blurb: Offset lithograph from the 1950s, when Andy Warhol was New York's most sought-after commercial illustrator. Authenticated by the Andy Warhol Foundation, it reveals the origins of his Pop eye: humour, delicate line and the commission turned into art.

warhol-gee-merrie-colour.description: A piece from Warhol's early career as a commercial illustrator for I. Miller. It captures the spirit of post-war fashion in a playful, elegant style.
warhol-gee-merrie-colour.blurb: From the period when Warhol drew shoes for I. Miller, the campaign that made his name in post-war Manhattan. A hand-coloured lithograph with his characteristic blotted line: an early document of the artist before the soup can.

warhol-gee-merrie-bw.description: Monochrome version from the Gee, Merrie Shoes series. A lithograph that demonstrates Warhol's mastery of line drawing during his years as an illustrator.
warhol-gee-merrie-bw.blurb: Monochrome version from the Gee, Merrie Shoes series. Without colour, the piece reveals the virtuosity of Warhol's draughtsmanship and his transferred-line technique, a direct precursor of the mechanical repetition that would define Pop Art. An intimate format, ideal for reading spaces.

warhol-tattooed-woman.description: Work not catalogued in Feldman & Schellmann. It depicts a tattooed woman holding a rose.
warhol-tattooed-woman.blurb: Offset lithograph from the mid-1950s, not catalogued in Feldman & Schellmann. A tattooed woman holds a rose: popular iconography and an illustrative tone that herald Warhol's interest in consumer imagery and mass culture.

warhol-flowers.description: Andy Warhol's iconic Flowers series. Halcyon Gallery valuation document.
warhol-flowers.blurb: Screenprint from the Flowers series (1970), one of the most recognisable images of Pop. Warhol started from a magazine photograph and turned it into a flat, repeatable, luminous motif. A square format of over 90 cm, designed to command a wall.
warhol-flowers.ref_note: An impression from the same Flowers portfolio (1970, 10 screenprints) is in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art.

akushov-party-line.description: Vyacheslav Akushov, a Russian artist associated with Sots Art, the movement that critically reinterpreted the iconography and visual language of Soviet Socialist Realism.
akushov-party-line.blurb: Collage, pencil and tempera from 1978, a unique piece. Akushov belongs to Sots Art, the Soviet answer to Pop, which appropriated official slogans and posters in order to empty them of meaning. A work rarely found in Spanish collections, with strong historical resonance.

akushov-two-lenin.description: A diptych that reinterprets Leninist iconography through the language of the Soviet poster. Executed on Gosznak paper, the same paper used to print Soviet banknotes and official documents.
akushov-two-lenin.blurb: A unique diptych on Gosznak paper, the stock used to print official documents in the USSR. Two variations on Leninist iconography and the language of the propaganda poster, reread with Sots Art irony. A conversation piece for corporate spaces.

bulatov-wanted-dark.description: Erik Bulatov (Sverdlovsk, 1933), a central figure of Russian conceptual art and the Sots Art movement. His work confronts Soviet iconography with pictorial space, creating a tension between propaganda and individual freedom. Represented at the Centre Pompidou, Tate Modern, the Tretyakov Gallery and MoMA.
bulatov-wanted-dark.blurb: Mixed-media study by Erik Bulatov, one of the defining names of Russian conceptual art. His work sets word against image, pictorial space against slogan, to ask what we really see. An original 2002 study for discerning collectors.

brandmeier-untitled.medium: Pencil, oil and tape on waxed paper
brandmeier-untitled.description: Monika Brandmeier (Recklinghausen, 1959), a German artist known for sculptures and installations exploring the relationship between space, form and material. Her work on paper shares the same sensibility: everyday objects translated into a subtle, luminous geometric language.
brandmeier-untitled.blurb: A unique work by German artist Monika Brandmeier, known for sculptures and installations that think through space and line. Pencil, oil and tape on waxed paper: a quiet, precise and thoroughly contemporary piece, perfect for understated interiors.

lashai-tyranny-autumn.medium: 22 hand-painted screenprints + original work on Plexiglas
lashai-tyranny-autumn.edition: Certified by the Farideh Lashai Foundation
lashai-tyranny-autumn.description: Farideh Lashai (Rasht, 1944 – Tehran, 2013), one of Iran's most important contemporary artists. A portfolio of 22 hand-painted screenprints plus an original work on Plexiglas from her installation of the same name, commissioned for the Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art (2004) and reconstructed by the Sharjah Art Foundation. The cypress as a symbol of Persian identity enduring adversity. Acquired from Edward Tyler Nahem Fine Art, New York.
lashai-tyranny-autumn.blurb: A portfolio by Farideh Lashai, a key figure in Iranian contemporary art: 22 hand-painted screenprints and an original work on Plexiglas, brought together as an artist's book. Poetry, nature and memory in a piece certified by the artist's foundation.

arroyo-payaso.description: Eduardo Arroyo (Madrid, 1937–2018), a key figure of Spanish narrative figuration and European Pop Art. Certified by Galería Guerrero.
arroyo-payaso.blurb: Watercolour and collage by Eduardo Arroyo, a leading figure of narrative figuration in 1960s Paris and one of the most incisive Spanish painters of the 20th century. His characters — boxers, painters, clowns — speak of identity and the mask with humour and critique.

castillo.edition: Original work · Certified by the artist
castillo.description: Jorge Castillo (Pontevedra, 1933). He took part in the São Paulo (1960) and Venice (1964, 1976) Biennales. His work is held by the Guggenheim in New York.
castillo.blurb: A 1985 oil by Jorge Castillo, the Galician painter shown at the São Paulo and Venice Biennales and held in collections such as the Guggenheim. A painting of intense colour and dreamlike space, certified by the artist, for walls that call for a statement.

derain-perfil.edition: Original work · Atelier André Derain stamp
derain-perfil.description: André Derain (Chatou, 1880 – Garches, 1954), co-founder of Fauvism. Certified by Galería Guerrero.
derain-perfil.blurb: A 1920 pencil drawing bearing the studio stamp of André Derain, co-founder of Fauvism alongside Matisse. After the explosion of colour, Derain returned to classical drawing: here, a profile rendered with economy and assurance. Small format, great name.

derain-cabeza.edition: Original work · Atelier André Derain stamp
derain-cabeza.description: Second Derain drawing in the collection. Certified by Galería Guerrero.
derain-cabeza.blurb: The second Derain drawing in the collection, also from 1920. A head barely ten centimetres across that shows a master's hand during his return-to-order period. Ideal for building a cabinet of drawings or a reading corner with character.

grau-garriga.description: Josep Grau-Garriga (Sant Cugat del Vallès, 1928 – Angers, 2011), muralist and innovator of contemporary tapestry. Held in the collections of the Metropolitan Museum and MACBA.
grau-garriga.blurb: Textile collage by Josep Grau-Garriga, the artist who lifted tapestry out of decoration and into contemporary art, with work in the Metropolitan Museum in New York. Threads, bobbins and fabric build a tactile surface in greens and ochres that brings instant warmth to a space.

miro-barcelona-iii.medium: Etching, aquatint and carborundum in colours on Guarro paper
miro-barcelona-iii.edition: Ed. 50 · Signed in pencil · Published by Sala Gaspar, Barcelona
miro-barcelona-iii.description: Joan Miró (Barcelona, 1893 – Palma de Mallorca, 1983), one of the leading Surrealists. Barcelona series (1972–73), J.J. Torralba workshops.
miro-barcelona-iii.blurb: A large-format print by Joan Miró in etching, aquatint and carborundum on Guarro paper, published by Sala Gaspar in Barcelona in an edition of 50. Carborundum lends relief and depth to the colour: Miró in his purest form, with his vocabulary of signs and his energy.
miro-barcelona-iii.ref_note: Another impression of the same print (H.C. proof) was auctioned by Setdart, Barcelona.

miro-barcelona-vii.medium: Etching, aquatint and carborundum in colours on Guarro paper
miro-barcelona-vii.edition: Ed. 50 · Signed in pencil · Published by Sala Gaspar, Barcelona
miro-barcelona-vii.description: Second Miró piece in the collection, also from the Barcelona series (1972–73).
miro-barcelona-vii.blurb: A companion to Barcelona III, from the same series and in the same technique: etching, aquatint and carborundum, signed in pencil. Together or apart, these pieces bring the colour, scale and instant recognition of the great name of Catalan Surrealism.

tracey-emin.description: Drawing by British artist Tracey Emin, a leading figure of European contemporary art and the Young British Artists.
tracey-emin.blurb: An original blue ink drawing by Tracey Emin, one of the Young British Artists who transformed British art in the 1990s. Quick, confessional, vulnerable line: intimacy as language. A unique, signed piece of enduring relevance.

tapies-visca.description: A highly symbolic graphic work in which Tàpies fuses his commitment to Catalan identity with his abstract vocabulary.
tapies-visca.blurb: A highly symbolic etching in which Tàpies fuses his commitment to Catalan identity with his abstract vocabulary of signs, letters and traces. A work with a story, particularly suited to institutions and spaces with roots in Catalonia.

tapies-gran-x.description: Etching featuring the recurring X motif, a central symbol in Tàpies's iconography.
tapies-gran-x.blurb: The X is one of Tàpies's most recognisable signs: crossing-out, intersection, unknown. In this 1976 etching it takes centre stage. Graphic rigour and symbolic force for offices, boardrooms and reception areas.

tapies-creu.description: A print combining the cross and the letter S, marks that move between writing and pure abstraction.
tapies-creu.blurb: The cross and the letter S, marks that in Tàpies oscillate between writing, symbol and pure form. A print from the 1970s that distils his idea of art as a wall on which signs and memory accumulate.

tapies-dues-mans.description: A graphic composition in which the 'dues mans' (two hands) emerge as imprints on the picture plane.
tapies-dues-mans.blurb: Two hands appear as imprints on the picture plane: a minimal, almost archaeological human presence. A print that sums up Tàpies's poetics, in which the body leaves its trace on matter.

tapies-esgrafiat.description: Sgraffito on a black ground, the scratching technique characteristic of Tàpies.
tapies-esgrafiat.blurb: Sgraffito on a black ground: Tàpies scrapes, scratches and uncovers the surface. A print of great intensity that carries onto paper one of the essential gestures of his matter painting.

tapies-espai.description: A space shaped by signs: numbers, letters and marks as vestiges of communication.
tapies-espai.blurb: Numbers, letters and marks organise a space that resembles a wall full of vestiges. A 1970s print about communication, time and the trace, ideal for spaces of work and reflection.

tapies-lletra-o.description: A graphic exploration centred on the letter O: pure form, void and circularity.
tapies-lletra-o.blurb: The letter O as pure form: void, circle, origin. Tàpies turns a letter of the alphabet into a contemplative image. A restrained, elegant print that works very well in series and wall groupings.

tapies-lletres.description: A composition in which letters dissolve into a grey atmosphere.
tapies-lletres.blurb: Letters dissolving into a grey atmosphere: writing that becomes landscape. A print of restrained tone and great delicacy within the collection's group of Tàpies graphic works.

plensa1.description: Print by Catalan sculptor Jaume Plensa, world-renowned for his monumental installations.
plensa1.blurb: A print by Jaume Plensa, the Catalan sculptor behind the large heads and letter figures installed in cities around the world. His graphic work pursues the same search: silence, the word and human presence. Vertical format, 76 × 56 cm.

plensa2.description: Second Plensa graphic work in the collection.
plensa2.blurb: The second Plensa print in this format, designed to converse with Grabado 1 in the same space. An accessible way to bring in the signature of one of the Spanish artists with the greatest international reach.

valdes-1.description: Original print by Manolo Valdés, published by Art of this Century in 2002, Paris.
valdes-1.blurb: Drypoint on chiné paper published by Art of this Century (Paris, 2002), numbered and signed. Manolo Valdés, co-founder of Equipo Crónica, rereads the great masters of painting in a language all his own. The first print of a series of ten held in the collection.

valdes-10.blurb: A print from the series of drypoints Manolo Valdés made for Art of this Century in 2002, in an edition of 75. The drypoint line, with its velvety burr, combines with chiné paper to give depth to his reinterpretations of art history.

valdes-2.blurb: Drypoint on chiné paper from the series published in Paris in 2002. Valdés takes icons of painting and rebuilds them with a free line and a Pop sensibility: a big name in a manageable format, easy to integrate into series.

valdes-3.blurb: The third print from the Art of this Century series. Like the rest of the set, it measures 51 × 40.5 cm, allowing walls of two, three or more pieces to be composed with coherence and rhythm.

valdes-4.blurb: Drypoint by Manolo Valdés, one of the living Spanish artists most widely represented in international museums and collections. Part of the 2002 series published in Paris; ideal for corridors, meeting rooms and transit areas.

valdes-5.blurb: A print from the same series of drypoints on chiné paper. Drawing directly onto the copper preserves the freshness of Valdés's gesture and his constant dialogue with the painting tradition.

valdes-6.blurb: The sixth print from the Art of this Century series. An accessible way to bring original graphic work by an established artist into a project, in a limited and documented edition.

valdes-7.blurb: Drypoint on chiné paper from 2002. Together with the other prints in the series, it allows a unified graphic installation, particularly effective in hotels and corporate spaces.

valdes-8.blurb: A print from the series published by Art of this Century in Paris. Line, paper and limited edition: an original work by Manolo Valdés in a format designed to live alongside architecture.

valdes-9.blurb: The penultimate print of the series of ten held in the collection. With its companions, it forms one of the most versatile graphic groups in the catalogue for interior design projects.

cuixart.description: Modest Cuixart, co-founder of the Dau al Set group.
cuixart.blurb: Mixed media on card by Modest Cuixart, who in 1948 co-founded the Dau al Set group with Tàpies, Tharrats and Brossa. Matter, gesture and colour in the tradition of Catalan Informalism, in an intimate format.

subirachs.description: Drawing by sculptor Josep Maria Subirachs (1927–2014), known for the Passion façade of the Sagrada Família.
subirachs.blurb: A charcoal drawing by Josep Maria Subirachs, the sculptor of the Passion façade of the Sagrada Família. His sculptor's thinking is evident in the drawing: volume, geometry and the synthesised figure.

raventos.description: Maria Assumpció Raventós i Torras (Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, 1930), Catalan painter and printmaker.
raventos.blurb: Graphic work by Maria Assumpció Raventós, a Catalan painter and printmaker associated with abstraction and Informalism. A female voice of the post-war generation that deserves its place on the wall.

tharrats-18.description: Joan-Josep Tharrats, co-founder of the Dau al Set group. 'Maculatures' technique.
tharrats-18.blurb: Acrylic on card by Joan-Josep Tharrats, co-founder of Dau al Set and inventor of «maculatures», a printing and stamping technique that produces unpredictable textures. The first piece in a series of compositions from 1990.

tharrats-19.blurb: A composition from Tharrats's 1990 series. His maculatures evoke cosmos, maps and matter in motion: experimental Catalan abstraction, in a 54 × 37 cm format.

tharrats-20.blurb: One of the 1990 compositions in which Tharrats explores the controlled chance of printing. It works alone or in series, bringing colour and texture to contemporary spaces.

tharrats-21.blurb: Acrylic on card from the 1990 series. Tharrats's work, halfway between painting and printmaking, is a direct testimony to the Catalan avant-garde born with Dau al Set.

tharrats-22.blurb: A Tharrats composition in which texture and colour are layered. Its format is consistent with the rest of the series, ideal for composing walls of three or more pieces.

tharrats-25.blurb: Another piece from the 1990 series: experimental abstraction, vibrant surfaces and the mark of an artist who made technique a territory of invention.

tharrats-26.blurb: Acrylic on card by Joan-Josep Tharrats. A work that speaks of energy, matter and chance, and sits naturally in clean-lined interiors.

tharrats-27.blurb: A composition from the 1990 series, in the same format as its companions. Together they form one of the collection's most complete offerings for projects with a Catalan identity.

tharrats-28.blurb: A piece from Tharrats's series of maculatures. Colour and texture in dialogue, with the experimental freedom that characterised the Dau al Set group.

tharrats-29.blurb: Acrylic on card from 1990. A painting that invites close looking: overlays, transparencies and controlled accidents.

tharrats-30.blurb: A Tharrats composition from the 1990 series. Together with the rest of the group, it makes it possible to create a room or corridor devoted to Catalan abstraction.

tharrats-32.blurb: The collection's only Tharrats on wood, from 1980 and in landscape format. The rigid support heightens the physical presence of the paint and its quality as an object.

bultrini.description: Matteo Bultrini (Rome, 1979). Certified by Galería Guerrero.
bultrini.blurb: A large vertical mixed-media work by Roman painter Matteo Bultrini. Contemporary Abstract Expressionism with references to landscape: a work of emphatic presence for generous spaces.

fernandez-capitol.description: Luis Fernández (1923–2012). Certified by Galería Guerrero.
fernandez-capitol.blurb: A 1976 oil by Luis Fernández depicting the Edificio Capitol, an icon of Madrid's Gran Vía. Urban realism at 130 × 100 cm: a piece with a city story, particularly suited to Madrid.

hurtuna.description: Josep Hurtuna Giralt (1913–1978), Catalan painter and printmaker. Certified by Galería Guerrero.
hurtuna.blurb: A 1969 oil by Josep Hurtuna, a Catalan painter and printmaker of the post-war generation. A generously sized abstraction that brings solidity and colour to offices and meeting rooms.

ribas.description: Lluís Ribas (El Masnou, Barcelona, 1949). Certified by Galería Guerrero.
ribas.blurb: A one-metre-square oil by El Masnou painter Lluís Ribas. A figurative, popular scene with the warmth of narrative painting: an approachable work that converses with its viewer.

cuixart-1.description: Modest Cuixart (Barcelona, 1925 – Palafrugell, 2007), co-founder of the Dau al Set group. Certified by Galería Guerrero.
cuixart-1.blurb: The second Modest Cuixart mixed-media work in the collection, an original and unique piece. The figure emerges from the matter, in the language the artist developed after his Informalist period.

rafols-acord-ombres.description: A large-format etching in which Ràfols-Casamada explores the tension between light and shadow through a restrained palette and balanced gestures.
rafols-acord-ombres.blurb: A large-format etching by Albert Ràfols-Casamada, painter and poet, one of the most lyrical voices of Catalan abstraction. Light and shadow are balanced in a restrained, serene palette: ideal for calm spaces.

dylan-two-sisters.description: A large-format print from Bob Dylan's graphic series. Signed limited edition.
dylan-two-sisters.blurb: A large-format print by Bob Dylan, in a signed limited edition. The Nobel laureate in Literature has drawn and painted for decades; his visual work shares with his songs the eye of a traveller and storyteller.

dylan-train-tracks.description: Part of the signed limited-edition portfolio by Bob Dylan. A landscape of railway tracks reflecting the imagery of travel so present in his work.
dylan-train-tracks.blurb: Railway tracks vanishing towards the horizon: the imagery of travel, so present in Dylan's songs, in a signed limited-edition print. A conversation piece for hotels and creative spaces.

opie-ika.medium: Inkjet print on Epson Premium Semigloss
opie-ika.description: A portrait from Julian Opie's Portraits series. Inkjet print on semi-gloss paper in a limited edition of 40.
opie-ika.blurb: A portrait from the Portraits series by Julian Opie, the British artist who reduces the human figure to line and flat colour. An edition of 40: a clean, contemporary image that works well in reception areas and brand spaces.
opie-ika.ref_note: Another impression from the same edition of 40 (Alan Cristea Gallery, London) was auctioned by Sotheby’s in 2024.

wesselmann-monica.description: A large-format screenprint in which Wesselmann fuses the contemporary nude with a direct reference to Cézanne.
wesselmann-monica.blurb: A screenprint nearly one and a half metres tall by Tom Wesselmann, a major figure of American Pop Art. The contemporary nude converses with a quotation from Cézanne: art history and pop culture in a single image.
wesselmann-monica.ref_note: Another impression of the same screenprint (Portfolio 90) was auctioned by Sotheby’s in 2024.

feito.description: An abstract composition in reds and blacks, characteristic of Feito's Informalist language.
feito.blurb: A print by Luis Feito, co-founder of the El Paso group and a benchmark of Spanish Informalism. Reds and blacks in tension, with the economy of means that characterises his mature work.

hartung.description: A work characteristic of Hartung's gestural language, with converging lines on a black ground and a yellow band of colour.
hartung.blurb: An original lithograph by Hans Hartung, a pioneer of European lyrical abstraction. Converging lines on a black ground and a band of colour: gesture turned into structure.

subirachs-las-meninas.description: A reinterpretation of Velázquez's Las Meninas theme in Subirachs's characteristic geometric, monumental language.
subirachs-las-meninas.blurb: A lithograph in which Subirachs reinterprets Velázquez's Las Meninas in his geometric, monumental language. A dialogue between Barcelona's great 20th-century sculptor and the most studied painting in Spanish art.

subirachs-a-david.description: A lithograph paying homage to the figure of David in Subirachs's characteristic geometric, monumental style.
subirachs-a-david.blurb: A lithograph by Subirachs devoted to the figure of David, rendered with the geometric synthesis that characterises his sculpture. Classicism and modernity in a 70 × 50 cm format.

paricio.description: Pedro Paricio (Santa Cruz de Tenerife, 1982), one of the most sought-after young artists on the Spanish scene. A large-format oil on canvas in his characteristic language of dense impasto and vibrant palette.
paricio.blurb: A large-format oil by Canarian painter Pedro Paricio, one of the young Spanish painters with the strongest prospects. Its title pays homage to Van Gogh in a language of his own: colourful and contemporary.

valdes-mariana.description: A reinterpretation of classical iconography in Valdés's own pictorial language, with figures emerging from glazes and ethereal textures.
valdes-mariana.blurb: Mariana of Austria, portrayed by Velázquez, is one of Manolo Valdés's signature motifs. In this mixed-media print the figure emerges from glazes and textures: art history rewritten in matter.

atchugarry.description: A marble sculpture capturing the upward movement and organic fluidity characteristic of Atchugarry's work.
atchugarry.blurb: A Carrara marble sculpture by Pablo Atchugarry, the Uruguayan sculptor based in Italy whose vertical forms seem to rise like light. Upward movement and a polished surface: a piece to be walked around.

grau-garriga-2.edition: Original work · Certified by Galería Guerrero
grau-garriga-2.description: A composition in which the figure merges with architectural space in Grau-Garriga's characteristic matter-based, textile language.
grau-garriga-2.blurb: Mixed media on canvas in which Grau-Garriga merges figure and architecture through his matter-based, textile language. A warm work with a rich surface, certified by Galería Guerrero.

grau-garriga-3.edition: Original work · Certified by Galería Guerrero
grau-garriga-3.description: A dark silhouette contemplating a green screen against a light background. A dialogue between the human figure and abstraction in Grau-Garriga's pictorial universe.
grau-garriga-3.blurb: A dark silhouette before a green screen: a dialogue between human figure and abstraction in Grau-Garriga's universe. Painting with a textile vocation, of great evocative power.

clave.edition: Original work · Signed · Certified by Galería Guerrero
clave.description: Antoni Clavé i Sanmartí (Barcelona, 1913 – Saint-Tropez, 2005), painter, printmaker and sculptor. Exiled in France, he developed a body of work between expressionist figuration and matter-based abstraction. Spanish Pavilion at the 1984 Venice Biennale. Gold Medal of the Generalitat de Catalunya.
clave.blurb: Mixed media on paper by Antoni Clavé, the Barcelona-born painter, printmaker and sculptor who built his career in France. Between figuration and abstraction, collage and gesture, his work distils half a century of modernity.

ribeiro-1.edition: Original work · Certified by Galería Guerrero
ribeiro-1.description: Alceu Ribeiro (Artigas, Uruguay, 1919 – Palma de Mallorca, 2013). Trained under Joaquín Torres-García. Represented in the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes in Montevideo and the Museo de Arte Contemporáneo in Madrid.
ribeiro-1.blurb: An oil by Alceu Ribeiro, a pupil of Joaquín Torres-García and a figure of Constructive Universalism. Everyday objects arranged within a geometric structure: balance, rhythm and a highly versatile earthy palette.

ribeiro-2.edition: Original work · Certified by Galería Guerrero
ribeiro-2.description: Ribeiro's second Constructivist painting in the collection. A composition of everyday objects reinterpreted in a geometric key inherited from Torres-García.
ribeiro-2.blurb: Ribeiro's second Constructivist painting in the collection, from 2007. Together with Bodegón constructivista I it forms an ideal pair for dining rooms, boardrooms and hospitality spaces.

hiro-ando-pandasan-1.description: Hiro Ando (Shikoku, 1973), contemporary Japanese artist and sculptor, a leading figure of Japanese Neo-Pop. His sculptures in resin, bronze and porcelain fuse traditional Japanese culture with manga and urban art. Vibrant finishes and iconic characters.
hiro-ando-pandasan-1.blurb: A sculpture by Hiro Ando, a leading name in Japanese Neo-Pop, blending samurai tradition with manga culture. Carved, painted and varnished stainless steel: humour, colour and craftsmanship in a unique piece.

hiro-ando-pandasan-2.description: Hiro Ando's second Pandasan sculpture in the collection. An explosive multicoloured finish on carved stainless steel. A unique piece of great visual impact for hospitality and corporate spaces.
hiro-ando-pandasan-2.blurb: Hiro Ando's second Pandasan sculpture, with a multicoloured finish on carved stainless steel. A playful, eye-catching presence for lobbies, brand spaces and creative offices.

plensa-twins1.edition: Workshop proof · Lelong Editions, Paris · Printed at Taller 46, Joan Barbará, Barcelona
plensa-twins1.description: Original print by Jaume Plensa from the Twins series. Published by Lelong Editions (Paris) and printed at the Joan Barbará - Taller 46 workshops (Barcelona). Certified by Barbará Calcografía.
plensa-twins1.blurb: An original print from Jaume Plensa's Twins series, published by Lelong Editions (Paris) and printed at Joan Barbarà's Taller 46 in Barcelona. A 100 × 70 cm workshop proof.

plensa-untitled.medium: Etching on handmade Korean Hanji paper
plensa-untitled.edition: Ed. 14/15 · Hand-signed · Certified by Polígrafa Obra Gráfica, Barcelona
plensa-untitled.description: A large-format etching on handmade Korean Hanji paper. Edition of 15 + 3 HC + 2 AP. An exceptional piece for its monumental scale and the quality of its handcrafted support.
plensa-untitled.blurb: A 178 × 125 cm etching on handmade Korean Hanji paper: an exceptional piece in scale within Plensa's graphic work. Edition of 15, certified by Polígrafa Obra Gráfica.

plensa-untitled1.edition: Ed. 11/15 · Hand-signed · Certified by Polígrafa Obra Gráfica, Barcelona
plensa-untitled1.description: A photogravure from Plensa's series of ethereal figures. Edition of 15 on high-quality Hahnemühle paper.
plensa-untitled1.blurb: A photogravure from Plensa's series of ethereal figures on Hahnemühle paper, in an edition of 15. A quiet, vertical presence, in tune with his large sculpted heads.

plensa-untitled2.edition: Ed. 11/15 · Hand-signed · Certified by Polígrafa Obra Gráfica, Barcelona
plensa-untitled2.description: The second photogravure in the series. A vertical figure in Plensa's characteristic language of glazes and dissolving strokes.
plensa-untitled2.blurb: A companion to Untitled-1: a vertical figure, glazes and dissolving strokes. Together, the two prints create a contemplative space well suited to reception areas and principal rooms.

plensa-monocrom.medium: Moulded paper pulp, polyester resin and black pigment
plensa-monocrom.description: A relief sculpture from Jaume Plensa's Monocrom series. Made of moulded paper pulp with polyester resin and black pigment, with a central form emerging from a dense, mineral texture.
plensa-monocrom.blurb: A sculptural relief from the Monocrom series (1990) in paper pulp, polyester resin and black pigment. A work from the period when Plensa was investigating matter and the object, before his large figures.

picasso-buho.medium: White earthenware with knife-engraved decoration on white glaze
picasso-buho.edition: Ed. 300 · Madoura Plein Feu / Edition Picasso
picasso-buho.description: Original ceramic by Pablo Picasso produced at the Madoura workshop in Vallauris. From the limited edition of 300, stamped on the base Madoura Plein Feu / Edition Picasso. The owl was one of the recurring motifs in Picasso's ceramic production.
picasso-buho.blurb: An original Picasso ceramic produced at the Madoura workshop in Vallauris, in an edition of 300. The owl was one of his favourite motifs in clay: a Picasso to touch with the eye.

picasso-corrida.description: A ceramic plate by Pablo Picasso with a bullfight scene. Catalogued as A.R. 182 in Alain Ramié's catalogue raisonné. Produced at the Madoura workshop in Vallauris, where Picasso developed a prolific ceramic output from 1947 onwards.
picasso-corrida.blurb: A ceramic plate by Picasso with a bullfight scene, catalogued as A.R. 182 in Alain Ramié's catalogue raisonné and produced at Madoura. Tauromachy, a central theme for the artist, in the form of an object.
picasso-corrida.ref_note: Another example of the same Madoura ceramic (A.R. 182) was auctioned by Christie’s.
